title: Mitosis Stages in Order Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
In the college lab, Diya looked at a slide of an onion root tip. Some cells had a plain round nucleus, others had dark threads lined up or pulled into two groups. Are these different cells, or one process caught at different moments?

You will see what mitosis is (equational division, karyokinesis then cytokinesis), a zoom ladder down to the centromere and kinetochores, and one cell dividing live through prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase, with asters, spindle fibres and the metaphase plate. Then how to spot each stage on a slide, prophase vs telophase side by side, a pause and think, six events sorted, the exam trap about the best stage to study chromosomes, an original NEET-pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions. This is Episode 76 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 An onion root tip slide
0:35 What is mitosis?
1:01 Zoom ladder: down to the kinetochore
1:28 One cell through mitosis, live
2:22 Spot each stage on a slide
2:50 Prophase vs telophase + pause and think
3:37 Worked example: six events
4:07 Exam trap: best stage to study
4:32 Practice question
4:54 Recap and three questions

Next episode: Cytokinesis and Significance of Mitosis. A plant cell has a stiff wall, so how does it split in two?
